name: Kazan State Medical University
highlight: One of Russia's oldest medical schools (founded 1814). WDOMS lists a six-year physician (Vrach) programme taught in Russian and English; the English-medium track is the one Indian students take. Six years plus the in-course internship clears the NMC's 54-month floor, but you still sit FMGE/NExT and do a further 12-month internship in India.

name: Bashkir State Medical University
highlight: Six-year physician programme with a Russian/English medium listed on WDOMS. Its programme is accredited by an agency recognised by the World Federation for Medical Education, which matters for ECFMG certification if you later want to sit the USMLE.

name: Kursk State Medical University
highlight: Long-standing destination for Indian students; WDOMS lists a six-year General Medicine programme delivered in Russian and English. Verify before you pay that your offer is for the English-medium stream, since the NMC requires the whole course, including clinical training, to be in English.

name: Volgograd State Medical University
highlight: Six-year Vrach programme listed in Russian and English. Accredited by a WFME-recognised agency. Its graduates are eligible to apply for ECFMG certification.

name: Tver State Medical University
highlight: Six-year physician programme with an English-medium track, roughly three hours from Moscow. Listed as currently operational in the World Directory of Medical Schools.

name: Tbilisi State Medical University
highlight: Georgia's flagship state medical university. The university's own admissions page prices the English-medium Medical Doctor programme at USD 8,000 a year (a separate 'American MD' track costs USD 13,500). The MD is 6 years / 360 ECTS with the internship built into the final year.

name: Petre Shotadze Tbilisi Medical Academy
highlight: Private medical academy in Tbilisi. Its own programme page lists the international-student fee for the six-year English MD at USD 7,000 a year (360 ECTS, taught wholly in English).

name: David Tvildiani Medical University
highlight: AIETI Medical School; one of Georgia's better-known private medical universities, with an English-medium MD accredited by a WFME-recognised agency. The university does not publish its tuition openly, so confirm the fee in writing directly with admissions.

name: Batumi Shota Rustaveli State University
highlight: State university on the Black Sea coast running a six-year MD in both Georgian and English. Listed and currently operational on WDOMS; accredited by a WFME-recognised agency.

name: New Vision University
highlight: Private university with a six-year English-medium MD (360 ECTS) and its own teaching hospital. Accredited by a WFME-recognised agency.

name: Caucasus International University
highlight: Private Tbilisi university offering the MD in Georgian and English, listed as currently operational on WDOMS and accredited by a WFME-recognised agency.

name: Asfendiyarov Kazakh National Medical University
highlight: Kazakhstan's oldest and largest medical university. WDOMS lists a six-year General Medicine programme taught in Russian, Kazakh and English. Note that on WDOMS the WFME-recognised accreditation is recorded against the seven-year Physician track, not the six-year one — ask admissions in writing which programme your offer is for and what its accreditation status is.

name: Astana Medical University
highlight: State medical university in the capital, with six-year General Medicine offered in Russian, Kazakh and English and WFME-recognised accreditation.

name: Semey Medical University
highlight: Six-year General Medicine degree available in English alongside Russian and Kazakh, listed as currently operational on WDOMS. The WFME-recognised accreditation shown on WDOMS attaches to the seven-year track rather than the six-year one, so confirm the accreditation of the exact programme you are offered.

name: South Kazakhstan Medical Academy
highlight: Medical academy in Shymkent running a six-year physician programme in Russian, Kazakh and English, with WFME-recognised accreditation.

name: Tashkent State Medical University
highlight: Uzbekistan's largest medical university (the former Tashkent Medical Academy). WDOMS lists a six-year General Medicine programme taught in Uzbek, Russian and English, accredited by a WFME-recognised agency.

name: Bukhara State Medical Institute
highlight: Runs an explicitly English-medium five-year MBBS alongside its six-year Uzbek/Russian physician degree. Five years of study plus the required 12-month internship clears the NMC's 54-month floor. WDOMS records the WFME-recognised accreditation against the six-year physician programme, not the five-year MBBS — confirm which programme your offer letter names and how it is accredited.

name: I.K. Akhunbaev Kyrgyz State Medical Academy
highlight: Kyrgyzstan's leading state medical school. WDOMS lists a five-year MD taught entirely in English (its Vrach programmes run six years in Russian/Kyrgyz). WDOMS does not show a WFME-recognised accreditation against that five-year English MD, which matters for ECFMG certification — get the accreditation status of your specific programme in writing.

name: International School of Medicine, International University of Kyrgyzstan
highlight: Bishkek medical school with a 5.5-year English-medium MD listed on WDOMS; long popular with Indian students. The WFME-recognised accreditation on WDOMS is recorded against the six-year Russian/English MD rather than the 5.5-year English track, so verify which programme you are being admitted to.

name: Osh State University
highlight: Its medical faculty runs MD programmes in Russian and English, listed as currently operational on WDOMS with WFME-recognised accreditation.

name: Kathmandu University School of Medical Sciences
highlight: MBBS taught in English over 5.5 years. Admission for Indian students runs through Nepal's Medical Education Commission entrance exam (MECEE-BL) and the Commission caps the fee — treat any agent who offers a 'donation seat' as a red flag.

name: B.P. Koirala Institute of Health Sciences
highlight: Autonomous health-sciences university; WDOMS lists a 4.5-year English MBBS, which is 54 months — exactly the NMC minimum — followed by the compulsory internship. Entry is via Nepal's MECEE-BL entrance exam.

name: Institute of Medicine, Tribhuvan University
highlight: Nepal's oldest medical school and the state university's medical institute. English-medium MBBS of 5.5 years; entry via the MECEE-BL entrance exam.

name: Nepal Medical College
highlight: Private medical college in Kathmandu affiliated to Kathmandu University, running a 5.5-year English MBBS. Seats and fees are regulated by the Medical Education Commission.

name: Manipal College of Medical Sciences
highlight: Pokhara college in the Manipal group with a 5.5-year English MBBS, long popular with Indian students. Admission is through Nepal's MECEE-BL entrance exam.

name: Dhaka Medical College
highlight: Bangladesh's most competitive government medical college. Five-year English MBBS plus a one-year internship. Foreign-student seats are filled centrally through the government's MBBS/BDS admission circular for foreign students, not by the college directly.

name: Bangladesh Medical College
highlight: The country's first private medical college. Five-year MBBS taught in English; foreign-student seats are allotted through the government's central foreign-student admission circular.

name: Holy Family Red Crescent Medical College
highlight: Red Crescent-run private medical college in Dhaka with a six-year English-medium MBBS listed on WDOMS. Apply through the government's foreign-student MBBS/BDS admission circular.

name: East West Medical College
highlight: Private Dhaka medical college with a five-year English MBBS, listed and currently operational on WDOMS. Foreign-student seats are allotted centrally through the government admission circular.

name: Enam Medical College
highlight: Private medical college at Savar with a five-year English MBBS and a large attached teaching hospital.

name: Yerevan State Medical University
highlight: Armenia's principal state medical university (named after Mkhitar Heratsi). WDOMS lists a six-year General Medicine degree taught in English and Armenian. The university quotes its international fee in Armenian dram, so get it confirmed in writing.

name: China Medical University
highlight: Among the first Chinese schools authorised to teach MBBS in English to international students; WDOMS lists a six-year English MBBS. Two cautions: WDOMS records the WFME-recognised accreditation against the Chinese-language programmes, not the English MBBS, and the NMC requires clinical training in English too — ask exactly how ward rounds and patient contact are handled.

name: Dalian Medical University
highlight: Six-year English-medium MBBS listed on WDOMS. The WFME-recognised accreditation shown on WDOMS sits with the Chinese-language programmes rather than the English MBBS. Chinese-language study is still needed for clinical clerkships with local patients — clarify both points before committing.

name: Medical University of Warsaw
highlight: Poland's largest medical university. The Rector's Order for 2026/2027 sets the six-year English MD at EUR 18,800 a year (EUR 112,800 for the whole course) — about USD 21,500 at July 2026 ECB rates. An EU degree, and the fees are published rather than negotiated through agents.

name: Poznan University of Medical Sciences
highlight: Runs one of Poland's oldest English-language medical programmes. The university publishes a total of PLN 485,000 for the six-year MD for 2026/2027 (PLN 71,000 in years 1-2, PLN 85,750 in years 3-6) and estimates living costs at USD 800-1,600 a month.

name: Jagiellonian University Medical College
highlight: The medical faculty of Poland's oldest university. Its School of Medicine in English publishes tuition of EUR 16,000 a year for 2026/27 admission (up from EUR 15,500 the year before) — roughly USD 18,300 at July 2026 ECB rates.

name: Davao Medical School Foundation
highlight: CHED-recognised medical school with a four-year English MD. Important: the MD alone is 4 years, and you cannot enter it straight from Class 12 — you must first finish a CHED-accredited BS pre-medical degree and pass the NMAT. The Embassy of India in Manila advises checking the latest CHED and NMC guidelines against the 54-month rule before you accept an offer.

name: Our Lady of Fatima University
highlight: Large private university near Manila with a four-year English MD. As with every Philippine medical school, entry requires a BS pre-med degree plus the NMAT first; the Embassy of India in Manila asks students to verify NMC compliance before confirming admission.

name: University of Perpetual Help System Dr. Jose G. Tamayo Medical University
highlight: A long-standing choice for Indian students in Laguna. The four-year MD sits on top of a BS pre-med degree and the NMAT — budget for roughly six years in total, and confirm the NMC position before you commit.
